title: When the E-NE Model Equals the Nested Markov Model for One-Arrow Bidirected Forests
banked_reason: D0.5 general referee: paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < field threshold 7.4; not salvageable within scope, while decision and math panels pass with no findings.
gap_reasons: The restricted graph family and absence of a worked causal application limit the result’s reach at a leading econometrics journal.
The fixing audits are not reproducible from the package, and the related-work discussion does not closely compare the obstruction motifs with published inequality classifications.
Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded, or re-anchor the proposal (rewind D-1.2).
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact equality-versus-strictness classification for finite binary, bow-free one-arrow bidirected forests, including support-zero response-table constructions and positive rational witnesses for all strict motifs. Decision and mathematics panels passed after primary-source citation attestation and repair of the enlarged-cut case split. The result remained below the field floor because its one-arrow forest scope and incomplete E-facet characterization cap its reach; fixing those limitations would require a broader successor project rather than a bounded repair.
tldr: For finite binary one-arrow bow-free bidirected forests, E/NE equals Zhao’s published nested-Markov model exactly when the arrow head has no nonleaf bidirected neighbor, or its unique nonleaf neighbor is adjacent to a leaf arrow tail. The same local rule separately classifies equality with the positive-closure nested model. Every other forest has one of three induced four-vertex motifs and a positive rational nested law violating an explicit E inequality.
gap: Zhao 2025 v2 proves E=NE and E-to-NM and asks about E/NE inequalities; Richardson et al. give the nested fixing criterion. Neither source gives a forest iff frontier or a boundary-law response-table representation. The chosen closed boundary convention makes the zero-stratum question precise.
fill: Establish or correct the proposed local criterion, prove the two division-free imputation formulas on every GM boundary law, and give three exhaustive induced four-vertex motifs with two E inequalities and positive rational nested witnesses.
